items.notes: Model not involved. The setting stays off by default (C-57). Builds only the safety part until the owner answers W15-112: the status and scaffold PR bodies carry a hidden ownership marker (the project's id, one form shared with W15-08); a project never pushes to, comments on or lists another project's status or scaffold PR; while another project's status PR is open on fr/status, this project writes no status PR (its status stays in the app, docs/status.md in its copy as today, and one log line says why); with none open, today's behaviour (fr/status, one PR). A legacy fr/status PR without a marker counts as this project's only when no other project on this install is linked to the repository; with two linked, neither writes to it or lists it. No per-project status branch and no second PR: both would change one docs/status.md and conflict on merge, which is the owner's question (W15-112). Amend ADR 0106 points 3 and 5.
check_changes: decision narrowed to the safety part (adversarial check spec_problems[0]): the earlier per-project branch fr/status-<project> and 'B has its own status PR' pre-empted owner question W15-112 and made two PRs on one docs/status.md

items.title: TR-1 has no fail-closed fallback: if Claude Code rejects a redacted built-in tool output, it silently passes the unredacted original to the model
items.root_cause_at_head: Holds at 931ed52: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:959-965 returns updatedToolOutput via builtInOutput(); packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:516-532 redactToolOutput walks every string; nothing checks the redacted value against the bundled Claude Code tool output schemas, and no deny path exists for a shape that would not validate.
items.notes: claude-agent-sdk 0.3.304 ships the built-in tools' output shapes only as TypeScript types (sdk-tools.d.ts, ToolOutputSchemas: BashOutput, FileReadOutput, GrepOutput, GlobOutput, FileEditOutput, FileWriteOutput, NotebookEditOutput, WebFetchOutput, WebSearchOutput, TodoWriteOutput, ...), no runtime validators. Never pass a resolved secret; R-readhook's 'no replacement when nothing is redacted' holds.

items.title: Changing the web search offer mid-run (max_uses down, or the tool dropped) voids the prompt cache: a quarter to a third of a research run's cost is cache rewrites
items.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live2-result.json research F3; model-calls-final.jsonl seq 9-10 (read 0, wrote 46,770) and seq 31-34
items.root_cause_at_head: Holds at 931ed52: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:563-583 recomputes maxUses every call from the money below the line; :632-643 leaves webSearch out when 0; packages/runtime/src/provider/anthropic.ts:280-282 appends the tool per call (its comment assumes the tools mark protects the cache); testenv/src/provider/prompt-cache.ts:96-131 ignores req.webSearch, so tests never see the rewrite.
items.notes: Keep the web_search definition (max_uses and the domain lists) byte-identical for the run while it stays affordable, and keep every limit in code: max_uses is fixed once at the run's start from the smaller of the task's searches left (ten over all its runs) and what the money below the run's wrap-up line pays; every call that offers the tool counts the full max_uses in its pre-call worst case; at the first call where the searches left or the money below the line no longer cover it (or the wrap-up was told), the tool is dropped for the rest of the run and never re-added: one cache rewrite, once, instead of one per call. No limit relies on text: a server tool is billed whatever the text says, and ADR 0107's guarantee that a search never eats the reserve kept to finish (fixup-web-search B1, ADR 0112 amendment) holds. Teach PromptCacheSim the API's web-search/max_uses invalidation. Amend ADR 0107 point 9 and the ADR 0112 note on fewer searches near the line. Avoidable waste per run is about USD 0.07-0.11.
check_changes: decision corrected (adversarial check spec_problems: 'enforced in the estimate and in text, never by editing the tools' dropped the code limit of ADR 0107/0112; verified at loop.ts:555-583 and ADR 0107 web-search point 4)
